name: Media Library Recovery – Restore Lost Images, Recover Missing Media Files
author: Krasen Slavov

sections.description:
Recover lost media library files with Media Library Recovery – the WordPress media recovery plugin that restores missing images after site migration, hosting transfers, or database restores.

Have images on your server but they don’t appear in your WordPress Media Library?

Media Library Recovery solves the common problem where image files exist in wp-content/uploads but are missing from WordPress database. After site migrations, hosting transfers, database restores, or development-to-production moves, files often get orphaned. This plugin scans your uploads folder, finds orphaned media files, and rebuilds WordPress database entries to restore them to your Media Library.

Whether you’re recovering from failed migration, hosting transfer, or database restore, Media Library Recovery reconnects existing files to WordPress without uploading or overwriting anything.

Why Choose Media Library Recovery?

  • Restore Lost Media – Recover missing Media Library files after migration
  • Fix Orphaned Files – Reconnect images on server to WordPress database
  • Media Explorer – Visual interface showing recoverable files
  • No File Upload – Only rebuilds database entries, never uploads
  • After Migration – Fix missing media after localhost to production moves
  • Hosting Transfer – Recover media lost during host changes

How WordPress Media Recovery Works

  1. Install and activate Media Library Recovery on your WordPress site
  2. Navigate to Media > Media Recovery in WordPress admin
  3. Media Explorer shows all orphaned files on server
  4. Select up to 10 images to recover (free version)
  5. Click Media Recovery button to rebuild database
  6. Check Media > Library to confirm WordPress media restored
  7. Repeat for additional batches of missing media files

Zero file uploads – plugin only reconnects existing server files to WordPress database.

Perfect For

  • Developers moving sites from localhost to production
  • Agencies migrating client WordPress sites to new hosting
  • Site Owners who lost media after hosting transfer
  • WordPress Admins recovering from database restore issues
  • Freelancers fixing broken media library after migration
  • IT Teams resolving orphaned media file problems

WordPress Media Recovery Features

Lost Media File Recovery
Scan WordPress uploads folder and identify orphaned media files missing from database. Plugin detects images that exist on server but don’t appear in Media Library. Common after site migrations, hosting transfers, staging-to-production moves, or database restores without file backups.

Media Library Explorer
Visual WordPress admin interface showing all recoverable media files. Color-coded icons indicate file status: existing (already in library), recoverable (orphaned files), selected (ready to recover), unavailable (cannot process). Browse orphaned files before recovery.

Database Rebuild for WordPress
Reconstruct WordPress Media Library database entries for orphaned files. Plugin generates proper attachment posts, metadata, and thumbnail references. Restores files to Media Library without uploading or overwriting – only rebuilds database connections.

Migration Recovery Tool
Specialized WordPress media recovery for post-migration scenarios. After moving sites between servers, databases often lose media references while files remain on server. Plugin reconnects these orphaned files to WordPress database automatically.

Hosting Transfer Fixer
Recover WordPress media library after hosting provider changes. When transferring to new host, file transfers may complete but database entries get lost. Media Library Recovery rebuilds database entries for transferred files.

Batch Media Recovery
Process up to 10 WordPress media files per recovery batch (free version). Select orphaned images, click recover, and plugin rebuilds database entries. Run multiple batches to restore all missing WordPress media library files.

Usage

Once the WordPress media recovery plugin is installed and activated:

  1. Navigate to Media > Media Recovery in WordPress admin menu
  2. Media Explorer displays all files in uploads folder
  3. Toggle Hide Existing to show only orphaned files
  4. Select up to 10 images to recover (checkboxes)
  5. Click Media Recovery… button at bottom
  6. Wait for WordPress database rebuild to complete
  7. Check Media > Library to confirm media restored
  8. Repeat process for additional orphaned files

Here are the steps to use Media Library Recovery:

  1. Open Media Explorer – Go to Media > Media Recovery
  2. View Orphaned Files – See all recoverable WordPress media
  3. Select Images – Check up to 10 files to recover
  4. Click Recovery – Rebuild WordPress database entries
  5. Verify Library – Check Media > Library for restored files
  6. Repeat Batches – Process more orphaned WordPress media

Note: Plugin scans wp-content/uploads folder and rebuilds database for WordPress. No files uploaded or overwritten.

WordPress Media Recovery Settings

Media Explorer Interface:
1. Access Media > Media Recovery in WordPress admin
2. View all files in wp-content/uploads folder
3. Color-coded icons show file status:
– Green checkmark: Already in WordPress Media Library
– Orange circle: Recoverable orphaned file
– Blue dot: Selected for recovery
– Red X: Cannot process (size/format issues)
4. Use Hide Existing toggle to filter orphaned files only

Recovering Lost WordPress Media:
1. In Media Explorer, select orphaned files with checkboxes
2. Maximum 10 files per batch in free version
3. Click Media Recovery… button
4. Plugin rebuilds WordPress database entries
5. Generates attachment posts and metadata
6. Creates thumbnail references
7. Restores files to Media Library

After Site Migration:
1. Install Media Library Recovery on migrated WordPress site
2. Open Media Explorer to view orphaned files
3. Select images missing from Media Library
4. Recover in batches of 10
5. All WordPress media reconnected to database

After Hosting Transfer:
1. Access WordPress admin on new hosting
2. Navigate to Media > Media Recovery
3. Identify orphaned media files
4. Batch recover to rebuild WordPress database
5. Media Library fully restored

Supported WordPress Scenarios:
– Site migration (localhost to production)
– Hosting provider transfers
– Database restore without file backup
– Staging to production sync
– Development site imports

Features & Limitations

The Media Library Recovery WordPress media recovery plugin allows you to:

  • Restore lost WordPress Media Library files after migration
  • Recover missing media after hosting transfer or database restore
  • Scan wp-content/uploads for orphaned image files
  • View recoverable files in Media Explorer interface
  • Rebuild WordPress database entries for orphaned media
  • Process up to 10 images per recovery batch
  • Hide existing Media Library files to show only orphaned
  • Display color-coded icons for file status
  • No file upload or overwrite – only database rebuild
  • Fix broken media library after site migration
  • Reconnect orphaned files to WordPress database
  • Batch process for recovering unlimited total files

WordPress Media Recovery Components

Media Explorer Dashboard
Visual WordPress admin interface for orphaned file management. Browse all files in uploads folder with color-coded status indicators. Filter to show only recoverable orphaned media. Select files for batch recovery processing.

Database Rebuild Engine
Reconstructs WordPress Media Library database entries for orphaned files. Generates proper attachment post types, metadata fields, and thumbnail references. Connects existing server files to WordPress database without uploading.

Orphaned File Scanner
Scans WordPress wp-content/uploads directory to identify files missing from database. Compares server files against Media Library entries. Detects orphaned media common after migrations, transfers, or database restores.

Batch Recovery Processor
Processes up to 10 WordPress media files per batch in free version. Rebuilds database entries, generates thumbnails, and restores files to Media Library. Run multiple batches to recover unlimited total orphaned files.

Migration Recovery Tool
Specialized recovery for WordPress site migrations. After localhost-to-production moves or staging-to-live transfers, reconnects orphaned files to database. Fixes broken Media Library without re-uploading images.

Status Indicator System
Color-coded visual feedback showing WordPress media file status. Green: already in library, Orange: recoverable orphaned file, Blue: selected for recovery, Red: cannot process. Quick identification of WordPress recovery candidates.

Known Limitations

Free version features:

  • File Types – Images only (All media types in Pro)
  • Batch Size – 10 files maximum (Unlimited in Pro)
  • Upload Path – wp-content/uploads only (Custom paths in Pro)
  • File Size – 2MB maximum recommended (Larger files in Pro)
  • Multisite – Not supported (WordPress Multisite in Pro)
  • Backup Folder – Not included (Uploads backup in Pro)
  • Search/Filter – Basic (Advanced filtering in Pro)
  • Priority Support – Community only (Direct support in Pro)

Detailed Documentation

Find step-by-step setup guides, video tutorials, WordPress media recovery tips, and migration troubleshooting on the Media Library Recovery Documentation page.

Media Library Recovery Pro

If you’re using the free WordPress media recovery plugin from WordPress.org and want Pro features, you can purchase the premium version on the Media Library Recovery Pro website.

Here are some features included in the Pro version:

  • All Media Types – Recover images, videos, PDFs, documents, audio files
  • Unlimited Batch Recovery – Process unlimited WordPress media files at once
  • Custom Upload Paths – Scan any directory beyond wp-content/uploads
  • WordPress Multisite – Full multisite network support for media recovery
  • Uploads Backup Folder – Built-in backup system for uploads directory
  • Advanced File Explorer – Enhanced search, filter, and sort for WordPress media
  • Large File Support – Handle files larger than 2MB with optimized processing
  • Background Processing – Recover large media batches without timeouts
  • Priority Support – Direct email support from WordPress recovery experts
  • Regular Updates – Early access to new WordPress media recovery features
sections.installation:
Installing the WordPress media recovery plugin is straightforward. Contact support if you encounter any issues.

Requirements:
– WordPress 5.0 or higher
– PHP 7.2 or higher
– Access to wp-content/uploads folder

Installation from WordPress

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New
  2. Search for Media Library Recovery
  3. Click Install Now then Activate
  4. Navigate to Media > Media Recovery

Manual Installation

  1. Download the WordPress media recovery plugin ZIP file
  2. Upload the wp-media-recovery folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  3. Go to Plugins in WordPress admin
  4. Activate Media Library Recovery
  5. Navigate to Media > Media Recovery

After Activation

  1. Go to Media > Media Recovery in WordPress admin menu
  2. Media Explorer displays all files in uploads folder
  3. Toggle Hide Existing to show only orphaned files
  4. Select up to 10 images with checkboxes
  5. Click Media Recovery… button
  6. Wait for WordPress database rebuild to complete
  7. Check Media > Library to verify media restored
  8. Repeat process for additional orphaned WordPress files

Quick Start:
1. Media > Media Recovery
2. Select orphaned files
3. Click Media Recovery button
4. Check Media > Library
5. WordPress media restored!
sections.faq:
Visit the Support Forum to share your questions or requests.

We usually respond to tickets within a few days.

Feature requests are added to our wish list and considered for future updates.

My images disappeared after migrating my WordPress site. Can this help?

Yes! This is the most common use case. After site migration, files exist in your uploads folder but WordPress database entries are missing. Media Library Recovery scans your files and rebuilds the database entries to restore your Media Library.

I transferred to new hosting and lost my WordPress media library. What do I do?

Install Media Library Recovery, go to Media > Media Recovery, and the plugin shows all files on your server missing from WordPress database. Select and recover them in batches of 10 until your entire Media Library is restored.

How is this different from WordPress backup plugins?

Backup plugins restore entire WordPress sites. Media Library Recovery specializes in recovering media files when they exist on your server but are missing from WordPress database – common after migrations, hosting transfers, or partial database restores.

Why can I only recover 10 WordPress files at a time?

The free version processes 10 files per batch to prevent server timeouts. Run multiple batches to recover unlimited total files. Pro version offers unlimited batch sizes with background processing.

Will I get duplicate files in WordPress?

No, Media Library Recovery won’t duplicate or overwrite existing WordPress image files. Plugin only rebuilds database entries for orphaned files missing from Media Library.

Is this compatible with WordPress Multisite?

WordPress Multisite support is available in Media Library Recovery Pro. The free version works on single WordPress installations only.

Which folders are scanned for lost WordPress media?

The free version scans only the default wp-content/uploads folder. Pro version allows custom upload folder paths for WordPress.

Can I recover all WordPress media file types?

The free version restores image files only. Pro version supports all WordPress media types including videos, PDFs, documents, and audio files.

Does this upload files to my WordPress server?

No, Media Library Recovery never uploads or overwrites files. It only scans existing files on your WordPress server and rebuilds database entries to reconnect them to Media Library.

What happens during WordPress media recovery process?

Plugin scans your uploads folder, identifies orphaned files, then rebuilds WordPress database entries including attachment posts, metadata, and thumbnail references. Files remain on server unchanged – only database connections are restored.

Can I recover WordPress media after database restore?

Yes, if you restored WordPress database from backup but files remained on server, Media Library Recovery reconnects those orphaned files to your restored database automatically.

My WordPress staging site lost media after database pull. Will this fix it?

Yes, pulling production database to staging often orphans media files. Media Library Recovery scans staging server files and rebuilds database entries to restore WordPress Media Library on staging.

Does this work with custom WordPress upload folders?

Custom upload folder scanning is available in Pro version. The free version scans default wp-content/uploads directory only.

Can I see which WordPress files are orphaned before recovering?

Yes, Media Explorer shows all files with color-coded status. Orange icons indicate orphaned files missing from WordPress database. Green checkmarks show files already in Media Library.

Will this fix broken WordPress image links in posts?

If images exist on your server but show broken in posts due to missing database entries, yes. Media Library Recovery rebuilds database connections. If actual image files are deleted from server, plugin cannot recover them.

How long does WordPress media recovery take?

Recovery speed depends on batch size and server performance. Processing 10 images typically takes seconds. Run multiple batches for large WordPress media libraries with hundreds of orphaned files.

WordPress Security Enhancements

  • Security – Added nonce verification to wp-pointers.php AJAX for CSRF protection
  • Security – Added nonce and capability checks to mlr_reset_settings() for WordPress
  • Security – Fixed missing translation functions for wp_die() permission messages
  • Security – Fixed missing translation for wp_send_json_success() in WordPress
  • Fix – Replaced string concatenation with sprintf() and proper escaping
  • Fix – Removed unnecessary esc_sql() from get_posts() query for WordPress
  • Fix – Changed pagination validation to absint() for proper WordPress integers
  • Fix – Added translation functions to all placeholder attributes
  • Fix – Made “Reload…” and “No more results” translation-ready for WordPress
  • Update – Added comprehensive file-level DocBlocks to 38 PHP files
  • Update – Improved code documentation for WordPress development
  • Update – All files validated with PHP syntax checking

1.8.0

Major WordPress Media Recovery Features

  • New – Dashboard Widget with media recovery statistics and quick actions
  • New – Onboarding notice for first-time WordPress users with quick start
  • New – AJAX handler for dismissing onboarding notice
  • Update – Improved WordPress dashboard integration with recovery status
  • Update – Better visual icons and styling for WordPress onboarding
  • Update – Compiled and minified CSS/JS for WordPress performance
  • Fix – JavaScript typo in mlr-admin.js for WordPress
  • Fix – Added proper escaping and sanitization for WordPress security

  • New – Initial WordPress media recovery plugin release
  • New – Recover lost Media Library files after migration

  • New – Support for WordPress image file recovery
